items.title: A holistic framework for enhancing the resilience of grassland-based farming systems to climate extremes
items.abstract: Grassland-based farming systems face increasing climate challenges. This Perspective presents a holistic framework to assess resilience, identifying trade-offs and synergies among natural, social and formal insurance strategies to enhance adaptability.

items.title: Selective extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using deep eutectic solvents
items.abstract: In this study, the development of an ultrasound method for extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using acidic deep eutectic solvents (UAE-DES) was investigated. Optimization of the extraction parameters, which include extraction time, temperature, and ultrasound power (UP), was performed using the One-Factor-at-a-Time (OFAT) experimental design, followed by HPLC-PDA for determination of total quantified phenolic content (TQPC). In addition, the influence of water addition on TQPC was evaluated. The Maximum TQPC obtained was 5.78 mg/g using ChCl: formic acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 30 min, 80% UP, 10% water), and 4.67 mg/g, using ChCl: tartaric acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 25 min, 100% UP, and 20% water). The obtained TQPC was 5- and 4-fold higher in comparison with 70% methanol and 70% ethanol extraction. LC–MS-qTOF analysis of DES extracts revealed diverse phenolic compounds, while the concentration range of compounds obtained was as follows: ferulic acid (0.86–2.47 mg/g), catechin (0.12–2.16 mg/g), p-coumaric acid (0.12–0.32 mg/g), naringenin (0.54–0.86 mg/g), and apigenin (0.15–0.91 mg/g). SEM analysis confirmed enhanced accessibility of lignocellulose in DES-treated samples. The sustainability of UAE-DES extraction was assessed using AGREE, AGREEprep, CACI, BAGI, and CaFRI green tools. The grade assessment of each tool resulted in scores: 0.63 for AGREE, 0.57 for AGREEprep, 65 for CACI, 82.5 for BAGI, and 72 for CaFRI, indicating a greener extraction performance of UAE-DES in comparison with …

items.title: The assessment of gastric myoelectrical activity between different stomach regions based on three-channel electrogastrogram signals: a pilot study
items.abstract: IntroductionPrevious studies have widely used surface electrogastrogram (EGG) signals to non-invasively evaluate gastric motility. However, it focused only on the assessment of electrical activity in a certain stomach region and lacked the analysis of interactions between different gastric regions. In the study, we aimed to assess the correlations of myoelectrical activity between distinct stomach areas using functional connectivity (FC) methods by three-channel EGG for the first time.MethodsThe study contained 20 healthy subjects and the dataset for each subject consisted of two three-channel EGG signals (labeled as CH1, CH2 and CH3; CH1 projected onto the region of lesser curvature, CH3 projected onto the region of greater curvature, and CH2 positioned the region between CH1 and CH3) with a sampling rate of 2 Hz acquired from three locations of stomach during a 20-minute period of fasting and postprandial states respectively. Firstly, the EGG signals were band-pass filtered into three slow wave (SW) bands by finite impulse response (FIR) filter, namely bradygastria (0.017-0.033 Hz), normogastria (0.033-0.067 Hz) and tachygastria (0.067-0.15 Hz). Secondly, we employed four FC algorithms (i.e. Spearman correlation coefficient (SCC), phase lag index (PLI), mutual information (MI) and coherence (Coh)) to calculate the connection strength of each pair of gastric areas. Finally, the FC strength between fasting and postprandial conditions for all subjects or the normal weight (NW) or overweight (OW) people and between the NW and OW groups for both fasting and postprandial states…

items.title: Quality evaluation of a traditional Chinese medicine compound preparation containing Rhodiola rosea, Astragalus membranaceus, and Carthamus tinctorius
items.abstract: ObjectiveWe aim to improve the quality control of Rhodiola rosea, Astragalus membranaceus, and Carthamus tinctorius capsules (RAC capsule) from the aspects of thin-layer chromatography (TLC) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), respectively, and the established quality control methods are suitable for their popularization and application in large-scale production.MethodsA TLC method was established for the identification of R. rosea, A. membranaceus, and C. tinctorius in RAC capsules. A HPLC method with gradient elution and UV detection was established for simultaneous determination of salidroside, tyrosol, hydroxysafflor yellow A (HSYA), anhydrosafflor yellow B (ASYB), and rhodiolin.ResultsThe TLC chromatograms showed distinct and reproducible spots for the RAC capsule samples at positions consistent with those of the corresponding reference crude drugs, while no interfering spots were observed in the negative control samples. The HPLC method demonstrated excellent linearity (R2 > 0.9991) for all five analytes within their respective concentration ranges with precision, stability, and repeatability; RSDs all below 2%; and average recoveries ranging from 95.07% to 105.61%.ConclusionThe developed TLC and HPLC methods are specific, accurate, and robust, providing a reliable quality control strategy for RAC capsules. The study supports the standardization of this herbal capsule formulation and establishes a foundation for further pharmacological research and clinical investigations.

items.title: Complementary techniques for investigating the molecular dynamics of uncrystallized water
items.abstract: Uncrystallized water (UCW) refers to the fraction of water in hydrated materials that remains uncrystallized upon cooling. Rather than forming bulk ice, this water retains molecular mobility even below the nominal freezing point. In polymers and proteins, UCW includes strongly bound water associated with specific functional groups and more weakly confined water residing in nanoscale environments. As a result, it plays an important role in mechanical behavior, structural stability, and biological function. Because UCW is heterogeneous, no single technique can fully capture its properties, and multiple complementary methods are required. This review highlights how dielectric spectroscopy (DS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), neutron scattering, particularly quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS), and terahertz and infrared spectroscopies each probe different aspects of UCW across distinct time and different sample sizes. We outline what each technique measures, the models commonly used to interpret the data, and how combining these approaches helps distinguish between “free,” “bound,” and “non-freezable” water. Studies that apply multiple methods to the same samples, with consistent control of hydration and temperature, are essential for developing a coherent and quantitative picture of UCW. This integrated approach is also key to translating UCW behavior into practical design principles for cryopreservation, pharmaceutical freezing, and biomaterials. Importantly, complementarity arises from differences in timescale and the distinct …

items.title: Optimizing rosehip form and concentration in a plant-based appetizer: balancing sensory acceptability with nutrient composition and phenolic bioaccessibility during simulated digestion
items.abstract: IntroductionDeveloping functional foods with high bioactivity often compromises sensory characteristics, making optimization essential.MethodsThis study evaluated the functional composition, antioxidant activity, vitamin content, microbiological safety, sensory acceptability, and phenolic bioaccessibility during simulated gastrointestinal digestion of a pumpkin–apple–honey–walnut appetizer enriched with 1%–5% of rosehip extract or powder. Data of the six formulations investigated were analyzed using two-way ANOVA (rosehip form × rosehip concentration) with Tukey’s HSD post hoc test, sensory scores were analysed with a linear mixed-effects model with assessor as a random effect.Results and DiscussionSensory acceptability (9-point hedonic scale) was significantly influenced by the concentration regardless of additive form. Rosehip levels of 1% and 3% maintained high acceptability, whereas 5% significantly reduced taste and texture scores. Significant form × concentration interactions were observed for protein, carbohydrate, fat, antioxidant content and vitamins A and E. Specifically, as concentration increased from 1% to 5%, vitamin A declined by 36% in extract-fortified samples and by 41% in powder-fortified samples due to matrix dilution, with powder consistently retaining higher vitamin A levels. Conversely, rosehip powder provided superior antioxidant content (1.19–1.33 mg/g at 3%–5%) compared to the extract (0.87–0.92 mg/g), whereas rosehip extract induced a more pronounced relative gain in vitamin E (15%). Simulated gastrointestinal digestion showed that total phenolic …

items.title: Comparative analysis of β-glucan content in single and multi-species medicinal mushroom powders with potential nutraceutical applications
items.abstract: Medicinal mushrooms are widely recognized for their bioactive compounds, particularly β-glucans, which are associated with immunomodulatory, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities. In recent years, blends of medicinal mushroom powders have attracted increasing attention due to their potential synergistic effects resulting from the combination of multiple fungal species and their diverse metabolite profiles. The present study evaluated the total glucan, α-glucan, and β-glucan content of four medicinal mushroom powders (Ganoderma lucidum, Inonotus obliquus, Hericium erinaceus, and Pleurotus eryngii) as well as four multi-species mixtures formulated from these fungi. Glucan quantification was performed using the validated enzymatic β-Glucan Assay, based on complete hydrolysis and enzymatic determination of released glucose. The results demonstrated a clear predominance of β-glucans over α-glucans in all samples analyzed. Pleurotus eryngii exhibited the highest β-glucan concentration among single-species powders (47.63% dry weight), while Inonotus obliquus showed the lowest value (8.99% dry weight). Multi-species blends displayed elevated β-glucan concentrations ranging from 42.73% to 47.42%, confirming the contribution of high-glucan species within the formulations. The low proportion of α-glucans in all samples suggests minimal contamination with reserve polysaccharides such as starches and dextrin. Overall, the findings provide compositional evidence supporting the selection and standardization of medicinal mushroom powders and blends as ingredients for fu…

items.title: Chitosan coating with Pickering emulsion of cellulose nanofibril/kaffir lime leaf essential oil for gourami fillets preservation
items.abstract: Gourami fillets (Osphronemus goramy) are susceptible to rapid deterioration during chilled storage. This study developed a chitosan-based edible coating containing a cellulose nanofibril (CNF)-stabilized Pickering emulsion of kaffir lime leaf essential oil (KEO) and evaluated its fish-preservation performance. A CNF concentration of 0.25% was selected as chitosan/CNF/KEO (ChiCK) stabilizer, and comparing with chitosan (Chi), chitosan/Tween 80/KEO (ChiTK). A ChiCK showed the highest zeta potential (57.00 ± 1.04 mV) and inhibition zones of 9.262 ± 0.639 mm, 10.306 ± 0.127 mm, 9.472 ± 0.824 mm, and 8.696 ± 0.260 mm against Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Bacillus cereus, and Staphylococcus aureus respectively. Its application on gourami fillet was able to suppress microbial growth with total plate count of 5.30 ± 0.05 log CFU g−1, 1.12 log units lower than that of the uncoated fillets by day 2 storage and remined below the maximum limit of safe level (5.70 log CFU g−1), although the treatment did not reduce weight loss by day 3. The CNF-stabilized KEO coating therefore had potential for preserving the gourami fillets during chilled storage (5 °C–10 °C).

items.title: Food safety knowledge, attitudes, practices, and observed food handling practices among licensed street food vendors in Tlokweng, Botswana
items.abstract: IntroductionStreet food vending plays an important role in providing affordable and convenient foods, yet food safety remains questionable. Despite Botswana regulations on licensing, hygiene and inspections, the informal nature of the sector limits regulatory oversight and inconsistent compliance with established food safety practices. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes and practices among licensed street vendors in ten selected wards of Tlokweng, Botswana.MethodsA quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted among 100 street food vendors using a self-administered questionnaire and a structured observation checklist to assess both self-reported and observed food handling practices. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Mann Whitney U tests and Kruskal Wallis H tests.ResultsSelf-reported awareness varied across food safety topics. Most respondents reported familiarity with basic food safety principles (85%), awareness of foodborne illnesses (84.5%), and awareness of the importance of handwashing before handling food (94%). Fewer reported knowing the appropriate storage temperature for perishable foods (57.7%), how to prevent cross contamination (55%), the recommended poultry cooking temperature (24%), and safe thawing procedures (48%). Practice responses show limited access to handwashing facilities (2%) and waste disposal facilities (3%). 61% reported wearing accessories whilst cooking. Attitude responses were generally favorable with 90% or more expressing favorable responses to regulatory adherence, but disagreements were present for training, reg…

items.title: Tests reveal why titanium additions do not fully prevent pitting corrosion in stainless steel
items.abstract: Stainless steel is widely used for its corrosion resistance, but it is not invincible. In environments containing chloride ions, such as seawater, pitting corrosion can occur. These pits often start at tiny particles called inclusions embedded in the steel.

items.title: Scientists demonstrate AI-designed enzyme for drug synthesis
items.abstract: The new RFD4-Proteina unified generative model for protein design—created by the Institute for Protein Design (IPD) in collaboration with NVIDIA—uses advanced AI to generate entirely new protein sequences and structures, achieving computational design success rates five to 10 times higher than previous models and generating candidates five to 10 times faster.

items.title: Designing better adsorbents to remove PFAS from water
items.abstract: A review by Tohoku University researchers identifies key molecular features that could guide the development of more effective materials for removing PFAS from water. The study is published in the journal ACS Materials Au.

items.title: Elusive uranium 'sandwich' molecule isolated after more than 50 years
items.abstract: In a study published in Nature Communications, researchers from The University of Manchester and Lancaster University have isolated and characterized uranocenium, the positively charged form of a landmark uranium compound called uranocene. The work shows that this long-sought molecule is stable, and that it behaves in a way that challenges how chemists usually think about bonding in heavy elements.

items.title: Scientists discover a plastic-eating “Pac-Man” enzyme with a surprising secret
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered a remarkable “Pac-Man enzyme” that helps bacteria devour certain types of plastic and may offer new hope in the fight against plastic pollution. Researchers found that several biodegradable plastics completely broke down in soil within about a year, while conventional plastic remained largely unchanged.

items.title: Scientists discover why a 100-year-old mushroom disease won't go away
items.abstract: Scientists have uncovered a surprising secret behind a mushroom disease that has frustrated growers for more than a century: It involves more than 17 species of harmful bacteria, not just one. The discovery could explain why treatments have struggled to stop the disease and open the door to more effective, eco-friendly solutions.

items.title: The “glue” holding your cells together has a surprising second job
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered that E-cadherin, a protein best known as the “glue” holding cells and tissues together, has a surprising second job: helping epithelial cells swallow nearby dead cells. Using live zebrafish and mouse embryos, researchers found that cells can dramatically reshape their lower surfaces to engulf cellular debris while keeping their upper surfaces stable, allowing protective barriers to remain sealed.

items.title: Scientists find evidence for two origins of life on Earth
items.abstract: Scientists probing life’s deepest origins have uncovered evidence that the first free-living cells may have emerged not once, but twice. The findings suggest a striking possibility: life may share one ancient genetic code, yet have undergone two separate transitions into free-living existence.

items.title: Just two drinks a day may be far riskier than you think
items.abstract: A major new study reveals that drinking just two alcoholic beverages a day is associated with a 1 in 25 lifetime risk of death from alcohol-related causes, challenging the idea that moderate drinking is harmless. Researchers also found no significant overall health benefits from alcohol, with risks rising as consumption increases.

items.title: Popular cannabis sleep gummies may have a hidden dark side
items.abstract: A cannabis-derived ingredient commonly found in sleep gummies may be more habit-forming than previously thought, with new research showing that repeated exposure caused tolerance and withdrawal symptoms in mice. Scientists warn that CBN may carry risks similar to THC, although its long-term effects in humans remain largely unknown.

items.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
items.abstract: Scientists have uncovered a surprising new clue to why the Mediterranean diet is so good for the heart, brain, and healthy aging. Researchers at USC found that older adults who closely followed the diet had higher levels of two tiny proteins, humanin and SHMOOSE, produced by the mitochondria, the energy-producing structures inside cells. These proteins have been linked to protection against heart disease, Alzheimer's disease, and age-related damage.

items.title: Scientists discover a hidden switch that burns fat and blocks new fat cells
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered that switching off a protein called Mitch makes human cells burn more fat and prevents new fat cells from developing. The breakthrough builds on experiments in mice that showed remarkable resistance to obesity and improved muscular endurance, raising hopes for a new approach to weight-loss treatment.

items.title: Neutrophil-to-prognostic nutritional index ratio and short-term mortality in heart failure: an exploratory association without demonstrated superiority over PNI, NLR, or SII
items.abstract: BackgroundSystemic inflammation and greater illness severity are associated with adverse short-term outcomes in heart failure (HF). The neutrophil-to-prognostic nutritional index ratio (NPNR) combines neutrophil count with the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), a composite derived from serum albumin and lymphocyte count that is influenced by inflammation and acute illness. This study examined the association of NPNR with 28-day and 90-day all-cause mortality in hospitalized patients with HF and assessed its replication in MIMIC-IV.MethodsThe analysis included 1,885 patients with calculable NPNR from the Zigong Heart Failure Database and 1,150 adult ICU patients with HF from MIMIC-IV. Log2-transformed NPNR was examined using Cox regression, Kaplan–Meier analysis, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and sensitivity analyses, including parsimonious and Firth-penalized Cox models. MIMIC-IV provided an independent clinical setting for assessing the direction of the association.ResultsIn Zigong, each doubling of NPNR was associated with higher 28-day mortality (HR 1.728, 95% CI 1.130–2.642, p = 0.012) and 90-day mortality (HR 1.684, 95% CI 1.124–2.524, p = 0.012). However, the expanded models included only 32 and 36 deaths, respectively, and the tertile-based estimates had wide confidence intervals. RCS analyses suggested nonlinearity at both time horizons. NPNR AUCs were 0.727 and 0.717, with no significant superiority over PNI, NLR, or SII in DeLong comparisons. In MIMIC-IV, the continuous association was borderline significant at 28 days (HR 1.112, p = 0.049) and not statisticall…

items.title: Camel milk preservation: matrix effects across conventional and emerging technologies
items.abstract: Camel milk supports food security, nutrition and rural economies across arid regions, while its commercial development is expanding towards refrigerated products, fermented foods, powders and functional ingredients. This transition exposes a preservation problem that differs from that of conventional dairy chains. Variable conditions before processing determine the initial microbial and enzymatic load, whereas the distinctive organisation of camel-milk proteins, minerals and dispersed phases alters treatment delivery, physical stability and quality retention. This critical narrative review integrates matrix knowledge with direct evidence on established and emerging preservation processes. Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed, CAB Abstracts and Google Scholar were searched for relevant studies available up to August 2026. The evidence reveals no simple hierarchy of preservation technologies. Cooling, controlled fermentation, pasteurisation and drying remain the practical foundation of camel-milk processing, but their performance is bounded by raw-milk history and by matrix responses that include aggregation, weak gel formation, oxidation and loss of powder stability. These constraints have stimulated interest in lower-temperature and non-thermal approaches that may widen the interval between microbial control and unacceptable product modification. High-pressure processing currently offers the most developed pathogen-specific evidence within this group, while the reported performance of UV-C and ultrasound remains closely tied to reactor geometry, energy distributio…

items.title: Growth trajectories in exclusively breastfed infants with clinically diagnosed food allergy: a prospective longitudinal cohort study
items.abstract: BackgroundFood allergy (FA) in infancy may be accompanied by feeding difficulties and dietary modifications during breastfeeding, which may influence early growth. However, longitudinal growth patterns in exclusively breastfed infants with clinically diagnosed FA remain incompletely characterized.MethodsIn this prospective longitudinal cohort study, 73 exclusively breastfed infants (30 with FA and 43 without FA) were enrolled at 4–6 months of age and followed through infancy. A total of 268 anthropometric observations were included in the longitudinal analysis. Weight-for-length Z-score (WLZ), weight-for-age Z-score (WAZ), length-for-age Z-score (LAZ), and head circumference-for-age Z-score (HCZ) were calculated according to the WHO Child Growth Standards. Growth trajectories were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with infant-specific random intercepts. Age was modeled continuously and centered at 5 months. Sensitivity analyses examined nonlinear age effects and group-by-sex interactions.ResultsMaternal dietary avoidance was substantially more common among mothers of infants with FA than among those without FA (83.3% vs. 18.6%, p < 0.001). In the longitudinal WLZ model, the estimated difference between the NFA and FA groups at 5 months was 0.423 Z-score units (95% CI 0.036 to 0.811, p = 0.035), with lower estimated WLZ in the FA group. There was no evidence of a group-by-age interaction (estimate = −0.011, 95% CI − 0.086 to 0.063, p = 0.763), indicating no detectable difference in the linear rate of WLZ change between groups. Sensitivity analysis did not support a…
items.authors: Jun Fang, Zhanzhan Zhang, Yuanfeng Zhong et al.

items.title: Beyond food safety: environmental and sensory drivers of organic food purchase intention in an emerging market
items.abstract: Background/objectivesFood perception encompasses a multidimensional evaluation of sensory, nutritional, safety, and sustainability attributes, yet the relative contribution of each dimension to attitude formation and subsequent purchase intention remains understudied in emerging market contexts. This study examines the relationships between five perceptual dimensions (food safety, naturalness, nutritional value, environmental concern, and sensory appeal) and attitudes toward organic food and purchase intention.MethodsData were collected via an online survey from 255 consumers using a non-probabilistic convenience and snowball sampling approach. Partial least squares structural equation modeling with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples was employed to test six hypothesized relationships.ResultsFive of the six hypothesized relationships were supported. Environmental concern, natural content, sensory appeal, and nutritional content were significantly associated with attitude, while food safety concern showed no significant association. The five perception dimensions jointly explained 64.5% of the variance in attitude. Attitude was strongly associated with purchase intention, supporting its central role within the proposed model.ConclusionFood perception operates through an integrated, multidimensional assessment rather than single attributes. The findings highlight the relevance of considering multiple food perception dimensions when examining attitudes toward organic food and purchase-related responses.

items.title: Phosphorus in Balance: Evaluating the Costs and Benefits of a Circular Economy Approach
items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive cost-benefit analysis of producing alternative phosphorus (P) fertilizers from recycled water treatment residuals (Fe-WTR) and cowshed effluents. The cost-benefit values of Fe-WTR are compared to the net costs of recycling P using a synthetic adsorbent (commonly used practice-layered double hydroxide, P-LDH) and the costs of commercial fertilizers. Dairy wastewater is used as a source of P. The cost of 1 ton P using the Fe-WTR process is €329. In contrast, synthetic adsorbents (P-LDH) incur significantly higher costs, amounting to €3329 per ton, underscoring the economic advantage of utilizing waste-derived materials. Adopting Fe-WTR fertilizer not only offers substantial cost savings by avoiding landfill fees (€40 per ton) and wastewater discharge fines (€500 per ton) but also reduces environmental impacts when compared to the use of commercial P fertilizers (non-recycled P). The Fe-WTR method mitigates eutrophication and pollution, presenting the dual benefit of cost-effectiveness and environmental protection, which exceeds the common P recycling practice (LDH). Our conclusions are based on production processes in Israel and compared to previous cost estimations at the world level, assessing the potential gain from such circular production of P globally. Recycling P from waste streams can be economically viable and environmentally preferable at small and large economic scales, supporting global sustainability goals.
items.authors: H. E. Ganem, I. Zohar, M. Litaor et al.

items.title: The impact of alternative recycled and synthetic phosphorus sources on plant growth and responses, soil interactions and sustainable agriculture - lettuce (Lactuca sativa) as a case model.
items.abstract: This research assesses the efficacy of two phosphorus (P) adsorbents as alternative fertilizers in promoting lettuce growth. A synthetic Mg/Al-layered double hydroxide (LDH) and an iron-based recycled water treatment residual (Fe-WTR), both enriched with P from dairy wastewater and added at three dosage levels. We hypothesized that the adsorbents' physicochemical nature will overshadow the biological efforts in the plant ecosystem to increase P solubility, impacting plant growth, nutritional composition, and metabolite profiles. Fe-WTR significantly enhanced lettuce biomass compared to LDH. Yet, elemental analysis revealed higher or equal P concentrations in the low-biomass LDH plants relative to other treatments. Phosphorus uptake appears to influence the assimilation of other nutrients that divided into two groups: calcium, magnesium, zinc, and copper with notable correlations to P and nitrogen, iron, aluminum, vanadium and manganese with low correlations to P. Conversely, P retained poor correlation with most metabolites whereas iron showed a higher correlation with numerous metabolites. Analysis of metabolites, encompassing carbohydrates, the Krebs cycle, amino acids, nucleic acids, and stress and regulatory pathways, revealed diminished levels in the LDH treatments. Overall, carbon assimilation (plant growth) was more effectively predicted by soil P availability (adsorbent type and dose) rather than by cellular P concentration, suggesting root signaling was at play, influencing carbohydrate translocation to the roots. items.title: Biogeochemical impacts on soil phosphorus and other macro- and micro elements solubility, ratios and forms during heatwaves
items.abstract: Increased frequency and amplitude of extreme heat events can affect soil temperature, and biogeochemical processes. High temperatures may have contradicting geochemical and biological effects on essential elements solubility and forms. Endothermic behavior of minerals and oxides results in decreased solubility with increased temperature, while bio-mineralization is stimulated in response to high temperature. To elucidate heatwave impacts on soil biogeochemical processes, we performed a controlled soil incubation experiment and a field survey. Wet and dry alluvial soil sets were incubated at background temperature (33°C) for two weeks and then, a sequence of three heat events was induced (41°C/33°C alternations, five days each) followed by two short events of extreme heat (48°C for two days). Most soil indices changed trends after about 25-30 days. At the first part of the period, P, Al, Fe appeared to reflect endothermic behavior of (hydr)oxides and minerals in the dry soil (i.e., sorbed P was likely dependent on Fe (hydr)oxides dissolution), while trends of Fe/Al in the wet soil followed the dissolved organic C trend. Phosphatases enzymatic activities fluctuated positively with temperature, emphasizing the activity of residual extracellular enzymes sorbed to soil particles (dry soil) in addition to living cells excreted enzymes (wet soil). items.title: Continuing Medical (Anatomy) Education Series: Organ Donation and Transplantation, a Means of Continuity of Functional and Independent Life and Living
items.abstract: Diseases and disease processes are key components of life and living. The understanding and appreciation of this axiom will impact greatly on the quality and standard of human health and life. The human body is bedeviled by a myriad of diverse and large spectrum of pathologies. These vary from hereditary, infectious, inflammatory, metabolic, structural degradation, genetic alterations, neoplastic, toxicological injury, ageing and trauma. All these reduce the functionalities of the affected organ/ organ system. There are established first line management strategies for these pathologies, however more often than not, they may not suffice. At this stage, the replacement of such organ becomes the only option for optimal quality of life or continuity of life. This can only be achieved through tissue and organ donation and transplantation. Over the decades, steady advancements are being made in the medical field of human tissue and organ donation and transplantation. Thus it becomes pertinent for students of human medicine to be well and adequately educated on the issues that relate to the donations of human tissues and organs and their transplantation. Such issues covered in this article include global statistics on organ donation and transplantation; historical antecedents of organ donation and transplantation; sources of organ transplants; tissue transplants; set guidelines and standards by The World Health Organization, The European Parliamentary Research Services and The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare Nigeria.

items.title: Effect of Quinoa Protein Concentrate in Particulate and Fibrillar Forms on the Physico-Chemical Properties of Quinoa Starch Gels
items.abstract: The current study investigates the interactions between quinoa protein—both in particulate (protein concentrate, QPC) and fibrillar (QPF) forms—and quinoa starch (QS) gels, and how these interactions influence the thermal, pasting, and rheological properties of the gels. Gels were made by adding three different concentrations of QPC or QPF to a 10% QS dispersion (10, 25, and 50% w/w of starch). DSC results suggested an enhancement of amylopectin thermal stability and an acceleration of retrogradation upon a cooling stage by the addition of quinoa protein. FTIR spectra indicated that QS and QPC/QPF mostly interacted through hydrogen bonds. According to rheological measurements, in contrast to the increased G′ due to the addition of QPC (50%), only a slight increase in G′ was observed due to the addition of QPF (50%). Notably, this study is the first to directly compare the effects of QPC and QPF on starch gel properties, revealing that QPC markedly enhances gel elasticity. These findings highlight the potential application of the optimized quinoa starch-protein-based gels as functional ingredients in plant-based meat analogues, where improved textural and nutritional attributes are critical.

items.title: Relationships Between Chemical Compounds and Sensory Properties of Virgin Olive Oil in the US and Israel: Development of a Prediction Model for Defects
items.abstract: Virgin olive oil (VOO) quality is defined by both chemical and sensory parameters. While the chemical parameters are objective and measured using instrument-based methods, sensory quality evaluation is based upon human panels, which can be subjective, have less repeatability, suffer from fatigue, and require long and costly training. Tasting biases could be minimized by a trained panel, but using humans as a testing instrument is inevitably prone to various psychological biases, stimulus-related factors, and carry-over effects. The objectives of this study were to evaluate instrumental methodologies that will assist the existing human panel in assessing the sensory characteristics of VOO and to develop chemistry-based predicting models for sensory properties in the oil using VOO samples originating from the US and Israel. Our results indicated that oil rancidity highly correlated with the contents of chemical components contents; 1-penten-3-one, 3-hexen-1-ol, (E)-2-pentanal, and 1-octen-3-ol are the major volatiles associated with rancidity defects (low concentrations of these compounds). Positive sensory attributes, such as fruitiness, correlated with 1- acetoxypinoresinol and hexanal, while bitterness correlated with pinoresinol, the aldehydic form of oleuropein aglycones, and the dialdehydic form of oleuropein aglycone. The random forest model suggested that luteolin, (E)-2-hexenal, 1-penten-3-one, and C18:0 are the most useful measurements in predicting the occurrence of sensory defects in the olive oil samples included. items.title: Synergistic effects of biochar and poultry manure on soil and cucumber (Cucumis sativus) performance: A case study from the southeastern Nigeria
items.abstract: This study explores the suitability of different biomass feedstocks for biochar production and their effects on soil health and crop yield. Two planting seasons were conducted, involving cucumber as the test crop and eleven treatments combining biochar and poultry manure. Soil analysis revealed initial soil conditions with high sand content and low pH. Poultry manure and biochar exhibited pH, organic carbon, and nutrient level variations. Significant differences in cucumber growth and yield were observed, with the longest vine length in plots treated with palm kernel husk biochar and poultry manure. Residual effects in the second planting season displayed similar trends. Soil pH, organic carbon, and total nitrogen remained consistent between seasons, while available phosphorus increased significantly in plots amended with goat manure biochar and poultry manure. Calcium, magnesium, potassium, and sodium contents also varied. Fruit length, weight, and yield were significantly improved by biochar treatments, with the combination of palm kernel husk biochar and poultry manure yielding the highest fruit weight. Correlation and structural equation analyses (p < 0.05) highlighted the relationships between plant characteristics, soil properties, and fruit indices, emphasizing the importance of nitrogen and phosphorus in supporting fruit development. The study suggests that biochar application enhances soil nutrients, crop growth, and fruit yields while reducing reliance on chemical fertilizers. items.title: Renal protective effects of natural honey on animal model of hypertension
items.abstract: Hypertension, also known as high blood pressure, is a leading cause of cardiovascular disease and premature death worldwide. Numerous investigations have established that hypertension can cause alterations in the cardiovascular system as well as renal structure and function. Fresh honey is consumed worldwide and is claimed to be highly medicinal and has therapeutic effects against a wide range of medical conditions. We investigated the renal protective effect of natural honey in in animal model of hypertension. Forty (40) male albino rats, with average weight (120 ±10 g) were administered with high salt diet, HSD (80 g NaCl + 1 kg of diet and 1% NaCl in drinking water (10 g of NaCl + 1 L distilled water) for 10 weeks to induce hypertension in the rats. Following confirmation, hypertensive male rats were randomly selected for the experiment. Twenty (20) albino rats (15 hypertensive rats and 5 normotensive rats) were divided into 4 groups, Groups A-D. Group A: (Normotensive Control) no administration was given; Groups B-D (hypertensive rats) received the following treatments. Group B was treated with natural honey (15 ml/kg), Group C treated with hydrochlorothiazide (0.15 mg/kg), daily for 21 days; while Group D received no treatment, until the end of the 21 days administrations. Blood samples were taken in the end, and renal alterations were assessed via biochemical and histopathological analyses. items.title: Quality and Flavor of ‘Aliza’ Fruit: A Unique Pomelo × Mandarin Hybrid
items.abstract: ‘Aliza’ is a new pomelo × mandarin hybrid (Citrus maxima, cv. Red Chandler × Citrus reticulata, cv. Ora) developed by the Israeli citrus breeding program at the Volcani Institute. Here, we aimed to characterize the quality and flavor of ‘Aliza’ fruit as compared to other commercial citrus fruit, specifically pomelo (C. maxima), grapefruit (Citrus paradisi), orange (Citrus sinensis) and mandarin (C. reticulata). ‘Aliza’ fruits have a similar size as grapefruits, but have a thinner peel and a unique yellowish/golden color. ‘Aliza’ fruits are completely seedless and have especially high juice contents. They also have a unique, highly preferred flavor, characterized by high sweetness and moderate bitterness and acidity, with strong citrusy and tropical fruity aromas. Sensory analyses conducted with the aid of a trained panel and an electronic tongue revealed that the flavor of ‘Aliza’ fruits is different from the flavors of other citrus species. Consumer acceptance and preference tests revealed that ‘Aliza’ fruit are highly appreciated and favored. The aroma volatile profile of ‘Aliza’ fruit was somewhat similar to those of pomelo and grapefruit, but very different from those of orange and mandarin. Overall, ‘Aliza’ fruits can be distinguished from other citrus fruits by their unique color, high juice content and exceptional, unique flavor.

items.title: Flavor release and stability comparison between nano and conventional emulsion as influenced by saliva
items.abstract: Flavour release and emulsion stability depend on volatile organic compounds' environmental conditions, food microstructure, and physicochemical properties. The effect of pH (3.5 vs 7.0) and saliva addition on stability and flavour release from nano and conventional emulsions was investigated using particle size, charge and Lumisizer measurments. Larger particle sizes were observed at lower pressures and in saliva-containing emulsions. At 1700 bar, nano-emulsions (below 150 nm) were created at pH 3.5 and 7.0 including saliva-containing emulsions. As was clear from the creaming velocity measurements, saliva addition decreased the emulsion stability by reducing particle charges and increased viscosity by more than 50%, especially when prepared at pH 3.5 closer to the isoelectric point of the used emulsifier β-lactoglobulin (pH 5.2). (5.2). Flavour release from emulsions was measured at equilibrium using a phase ratio variation to determine partition coefficients and dynamically using an electronic nose. Partition coefficients of the flavour compounds for most conditions were two to four times lower in emulsions prepared at pH 7.0 than at pH 3.5 and in emulsions without saliva. Emulsions prepared with higher pressures showed stronger flavor release rates, while additional salvia dropped the release rate for ethyl acetate at pH 3.5. The physicochemical properties of flavour compounds, saliva addition and pH of emulsions influenced flavour release more than homogenization pressures.
